item.title: Amgen Tavneos Liver Toxicity
item.description:
• Summary: Amgen's rare disease drug Tavneos (avacopan) has been linked to liver toxicity and at least 20 deaths in Japan, according to reports. Amgen stands by the drug, which is approved for ANCA-associated vasculitis, citing its benefit-risk profile.
  • MoAs: Tavneos (avacopan) is a complement 5a receptor (C5aR) antagonist that blocks the pro-inflammatory complement pathway, reducing neutrophil activation and vascular damage.
  • Sources: Endpoints News, BioSpace

item.title: BioMarin Inozyme Flop
item.description:
• Summary: BioMarin's $270 million bet on Inozyme appears troubled after Inozyme's rare disease drug missed its key Phase 3 endpoint. The drug was being developed for a rare genetic condition, potentially related to ENPP1 deficiency. The failure raises questions about BioMarin's investment strategy and the future of the program.
  • MoAs: N/A (drug not specified; Inozyme's pipeline includes INZ-701, an ENPP1 enzyme replacement therapy).
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech
